primary_topics: Address introducing CJ Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno as the 24th Chief Justice of the Philippines, September 18, 2012 -- a day before the Ateneo FLP professorial chair inaugural (SD087)

The granddaughter Nicole Manalac anecdote: CJP's eight-year-old granddaughter, hearing of Sereno's appointment, brought blueberry muffins she baked and said she would no longer take up law since she can no longer be the first lady chief justice; CJP's reply: 'you can be the first baker in the world to become chief justice'
How CJP met Sereno and introduced her to President Aquino at the GMA7 60th anniversary (July 30, 2010) at the Makati Shangri-La, leading to her appointment as P-Noy's first SC appointee

Generational change: youngest associate justice at 50 under the 1987 Constitution; 20 total years in the Court; 18 as first woman CJ; CJP's hope to be alive at 93 when she retires to witness a 'transparent, accountable, excellent and trustworthy judiciary'
sub_topics: Nicole Manalac opener: CJP's eight-year-old granddaughter snuggled to him when Sereno's appointment was announced; brought blueberry muffins she baked; said 'Lolo, I am sorry I will no longer take up law and will just be a baker because I can no longer be the first lady chief justice of our country'; CJP: 'That is alright, hija, you can be the first baker in the world to become chief justice'

President Ramos tribute: CJP owes his SC appointment to Ramos; the private one-on-one; offered Secretary of Justice (declined -- 'I did not campaign for him'); 'I know that. I know also that you did not even vote for me. You voted for your mentor, Jovy Salonga. But I want to be President not only of those who voted for me but also of those who did not, but who are competent and honest'; 'President Ramos never spoke with me about any matter in the Supreme Court, even when I voted against some of his projects. Such is the gentleman that he is.'

Senator Drilon's delicadeza: President Aquino 'would have been comfortable to see him aspire for Chief Justice but Senator Drilon respectfully declined saying he felt awkward gunning for the post, after actively participating in the impeachment trial of the previous occupant'

Senator Angara's 1982 declination: when still UP President in 1982, Marcos offered him Chief Justice; 'also respectfully declined because he wanted to honor the tradition of having only insiders as Chiefs'

First meeting with Sereno: via retired Justice Florentino Feliciano who brought her to CJP's home; consulting on pending NAIA Terminal III arbitration cases in Washington and Singapore; 'Professor Sereno, as she was addressed then, struck me as a passionate and knowledgeable advocate who had complete mastery of the facts and the intricate laws involved'

GMA7 60th anniversary introduction: July 30, 2010, Makati Shangri-La; Sereno asked CJP to introduce her to President Aquino; CJP introduced her as 'a super lawyer-economist who could propel the President's program to the judiciary'; Sereno added: 'Mr. President, I met you a few years back. When you were still a senator, I briefed you on the pending ratification of JPEPA. The President lighted up and replied, Ah, yes, I remember now, and I followed your advice.'; 'After P-Noy winked at me, I felt she instantly won the President's nod'; appointed a few days later as P-Noy's first SC appointee

Generational change: at 50, youngest associate justice under the 1987 Constitution; 20 total years in SC; for 18 of those 20 years, first woman CJ; second in length of service only to Cayetano Arellano (19 years, 1901-1920); 12th in SC seniority totem -- 'most junior associate justice to become chief'; chief during terms of four presidents (Aquino, and winners of 2016, 2022 and 2028)
Insider-outsider balance: insider for two years (knows internal dynamics); outsider enough to see afresh, think outside the box, transform without being tied to past practices

CJP's hope: 'to be alive 18 years from now when I would be 93 years old, and she, at age 70, would be retiring and proudly bequeathing to our country... a truly transparent, accountable, excellent and trustworthy judiciary'

This intimate account of the appointment's informal backstory is unique to this speech.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered September 18, 2012 as an introduction of CJ Maria Lourdes P.A. Sereno as the 24th Chief Justice of the Philippines, this address by CJP opens with the most charming anecdote in the corpus: his eight-year-old granddaughter Nicole Manalac brought homemade blueberry muffins and said she would 'no longer take up law and will just be a baker because I can no longer be the first lady chief justice'; CJP replied: 'you can be the first baker in the world to become chief justice.' He greets President Fidel Ramos with the most personal Ramos tribute in the corpus: 'I owe my SC appointment to him'; during the 1992 one-on-one, Ramos acknowledged 'I know you did not even vote for me -- you voted for your mentor, Jovy Salonga -- but I want to be President not only of those who voted for me'; and crucially: 'President Ramos never spoke with me about any matter in the Supreme Court, even when I voted against some of his projects. Such is the gentleman that he is.' He praises Senator Drilon for declining the CJ aspirations out of delicadeza (after participating in the previous occupant's impeachment trial) and Senator Angara for declining Marcos's 1982 CJ offer to honor the insider tradition. He accounts for his role in Sereno's appointment: he first met her when retired Justice Florentino Feliciano brought her to his home for the NAIA Terminal III arbitration consultation; on July 30, 2010 at the GMA7 60th anniversary at the Makati Shangri-La, he introduced her to President Aquino as 'a super lawyer-economist'; Sereno reminded P-Noy of her JPEPA briefing; 'After P-Noy winked at me, I felt she instantly won the President's nod.' She was appointed a few days later as P-Noy's first SC appointee. He describes the generational change: youngest associate justice at 50 under the 1987 Constitution; 20 total years in the SC; 18 as first woman CJ (second only to Cayetano Arellano's 19 years); 12th in seniority and the most junior to become chief; chief during four presidential terms. The insider-outsider balance makes her ideal for reform. He closes: 'my hope and dream is to be alive 18 years from now when I would be 93 years old, and she, at age 70, would be retiring and proudly bequeathing to our country a truly transparent, accountable, excellent and trustworthy judiciary.'
